text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Conflict between government and Bundesbank over Finance Minister Theo Waigel's proposals to reevaluate gold and curreny reserves. Coalition supports Waigel. Opposition call for his resignation
- Hundreds of thousands celebrate victory of Borussia Dortmund in European Cup in Munich on Wednesday

- Health Minister Horst Seehofer declared his health reform law is ready. The minister addresses doctors conference. In the long term alternatives means of financing health system needed apart from state social insurance scheme

- Employers and members of the HBV white collar workers union reached agreement on sick pay overnight. They agreed on full sick pay for the 460,000 workers in the private banking sector and to an increase in pay from December of two percent
- Export remains a reliable support for the German economy
- Germany's DGB trades union federation want subject of unemployment to be at heart of EU summit in Amsterdam next month
- Machine-building industry continues its recovery, according to the German VDMA machine and plant building association
HANDELSBLATT

- Storm of indignation in the financial work about the Bonn coalition's plans to reevaluate gold reserves. Finance Minister Theo Waigel comes under increasing pressure. He wants to push through the new valuation of Bundesbank gold reserves despite huge opposition
- Life assurance profits are expected to increase, Allianz says. And also that no claims from Holocaust victims have been found to be valid
- Karstadt chief presents a new concept for restructuring
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG

- Bonn opposition calls for Finance Minister Theo Waigel's resignation. SPD parliamentary leader Rudolf Scharping said that the finance minister was no longer acceptable. Next work opposition SPD propose resolution in German Bundestag lower house on his resignation
- Bundesbank council members, Ernst Welteke, warns that reevaulation would reduce credibility of German government and the German central bank, the Bundesbank
DIE WELT

- Opposition in Bonn parliament apply for Finance Minister Theo Waigel's resignation. Vote on their resolution next week in the German Bundestag lower house of parliament. Government rejects Bundesbank's criticism of gold plans
- PDS reform communists in former East Germany keep status as opposition in Saxony-Anhalt state
- Finance world in turmoil over Finance Minister Theo Waigel's proposals to reevaluate gold reserves. Speculation over resignation of Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer
- The opening of German telecommunications market drags its heels
